findings.title: Remote import lets the chat model forge person edits, including person-only ones
findings.claim: `planroom import` takes the author from a local directory path that the chat model writes. It sits in the agent-callable `room_change` tool and allows person-only commands for the owner's uid. So an agent can turn its own proposals into person-accepted decisions without the person key, which skips the actor rules (DR-4) completely.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:237 puts `scan`, `import` under actor `any`, tool `room_change`. contracts.md:790: "the actor is `person:artifact:<uid>` from the path, never from the body ... person-only commands from the Artifact are allowed for the owner's own uid". architecture.md:1147: `/room sync` "returns `context` asking the model to run `ArtifactData list` on `inbox` with `out_dir: .planroom/share/inbox` ... It then runs `planroom import .planroom/share/inbox`". So the path is a local directory the model fills in. architecture.md:1093 and DR-4 (decisions.md:152): the `tool.check` guard protects only `person.key` and `serve.json`, not the inbox directory. This conflicts with KICKOFF R5 ("nothing the AI invents counts until a person accepts it"), R8 (merges follow a person's approval), and architecture.md:1091 ("Person-only commands aren't reachable through tools at all"). The `{self}` path is proof of authorship only inside the claude.ai db (artifact-spike Implications). Once rows are copied to local disk, that proof is gone.
findings.failure_scenario: In a turn, the planning partner uses Write to create `.planroom/share/inbox/<owner-uid>/events/x.json` with `{format:"planroom.inbox/v1", command:"decide", request:{id:CARD, choice:"accept"}, base:SEQ}` and then calls `room_change {command:"import"}`. The engine commits a person-attributed acceptance of the model's own ghost batch, and `s03_plan.rs::agent_accept_is_person_required` still passes because that test only covers the direct path. The same route can reach any other person-only leaf the inbox accepts, such as `intent version`, and a hand-off approval if the command allow-list doesn't exclude it.
findings.proposed_fix: Make import of `planroom.inbox/v1` rows person-only: it needs the person key, so only a typed `/room sync` or the pane's `t` press can run it. Take import out of `room_change`. Extend the `tool.check` guard to deny Write, Edit and Bash on `.planroom/share/inbox/**`. Keep a closed allow-list of inbox commands (`edit`, `decide` on a card in the published snapshot, `intent propose`), and turn any other person-only request from the inbox into a local card. Add a test where an agent-written inbox file is refused with `person_required`.

findings.title: A bare digit at the empty prompt can run an irreversible person action
findings.claim: The band's primary Button is the engine's next best action with hotkey `1`, and a bare digit typed into an empty composer presses it. Nothing limits `next` to undoable actions. Once a hand-off is collected, the natural next action is `handoff merge`, so one stray keystroke at the start of a message ("1. fix ...") merges branches into the user's repos with no undo.
findings.evidence: mod-spike.md row 18: "A bare digit at the empty prompt presses the mod's band Button". architecture.md:1081: band "next best action as a primary Button with hotkey `1`, `2` for the alternative and `3` for later". contracts.md:423 `next: Handle` is unconstrained, and pack `[[suggestions]]` take any `action` (architecture.md:499). contracts.md:195 `Undo::NotUndoable` exists, and the S15 undo assert (feature_list S15) covers "every Op x target kind, plus review, decision pick, version and claim", which excludes `handoff merge`. KICKOFF principle 1: "Everything is reversible, which is what makes bold defaults safe."
findings.failure_scenario: After `handoff collect`, the band shows "[1] Merge worker-status-via-api". The person starts typing "1) also check the gift-wrap change" into the empty prompt. The `1` presses the band Button with the person key, `handoff merge` preflights and merges `planroom/worker-status-via-api` into worker and platform, and the rest of the text goes to the composer. The merge can't be undone from Planroom.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a rule in the catalogue, checked by a test, that `PaneModel.next` and every band Button may only point at commands whose `undo` isn't `NotUndoable` and whose class isn't `handoff`. Show irreversible steps (merge, hand-off start) as a band label that opens the pane card, so confirming takes a deliberate second key, which still fits S9's two keystrokes. Add `band_next_is_undoable` to `keys.test.tsx`.

findings.title: Actions the surfaces depend on have no command in the one catalogue (`review`, `open`)
findings.claim: The design relies on a `review accept|reject` verb and an `open` command, but neither is a leaf in the `Command` enum. The enum generates the CLI, the HTTP routes, the tools and `/room`, so the pane's `y`/`n`, accepting ghosts item by item, confirming or rejecting inferred facts (R2), the conflict card's "yours", and the pane's `e` canvas login have no generated command to call.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:200-213 lists every `Command` variant: there is no `Review` and no `Open`. architecture.md:327-328: Confirmation is "`review accept` on an inferred edge", and ghosts are excluded "until a person's `review accept`". architecture.md:410: choosing "yours" is a `review accept`. architecture.md:881: "Accepting is person-only, item by item or as a batch (S3)". architecture.md:1075: pane `y` accept, `n` reject. architecture.md:1049 and DR-29: "`planroom open` (the pane's `e` key) prints `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/#code=...`". architecture.md:153 cites `/room open`, but contracts.md:736 ROOM_COMMANDS lists only leaves plus `/room`, `/room share`, `/room sync`. architecture.md:1008: "A test asserts every variant has exactly one handler". KICKOFF R2 says a person can confirm or reject any inferred fact, and S15 has "Every edit type has an undo test", which includes review (feature_list S15 asserts).
findings.failure_scenario: In the S9 live run, the person presses `y` on a pending ghost diff. The pane has no catalogue leaf to run, because `decide ID CHOICE` works only on a card. On the canvas, an evidence popover's "Confirm" for an inferred `infer` machine edge has no HTTP route. Pressing `e` can't print the one-time login URL, so the local canvas can't be opened from the mod. S4 step 1's evidence path ("the regroup ... on the canvas") stalls at login.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `review ID accept|reject [--cause C]` (idea Decisions, person-only, `undo: Edit`, `needs_base`) and `open [--print]` (idea Setup; starts `serve --detach` if needed and prints the code URL; `room: true`) to `Command`. Map the pane's `y`/`n`, the batch card, the conflict card and the canvas popovers to `review`. Add both to `room_commands_snapshot` and the undo matrix.

findings.title: "Two keystrokes from pane focus" holds only for the top item; the hotkey pool is spent
findings.claim: Pane actions act on the focused list row or the first diff, and the rows have no hotkeys. Reaching row N takes N arrow presses (or N `d` presses for diffs), so many main-flow actions take three or more keystrokes from pane focus. The planned test counts keys from the key map, so it can't catch this. Also, `ctrl+x tab` focuses the band, not the pane, so one of the two claimed entry routes is wrong.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1072-1079 assigns 20 letters (z x l p a o i d y n f w m s h g u e c t) and digits 1-4, with list rows on "arrows, `Enter` opens". That leaves only b j k q r v and 0,5-9, which is 12 hotkeys, for about 15 to 17 list rows at 49×34 and more on wider docks. mod-api.md:158 caps a site at "at most 36 one-key actions per pane". mod-spike.md:30 says "List rows and secondary actions use letters", but the letters are taken by actions. mod-spike.md:19: "`ctrl+x tab` Focuses the band". architecture.md:1081 claims "any pane action is two (`/room` or `ctrl+x tab`, then one hotkey)". The feature_list S9 test is "a keystroke-count table generated from the pane's key map". KICKOFF S9: "Every action is at most two keystrokes from pane focus."
findings.failure_scenario: In the S9 live evidence, accepting the third pending diff is `d d y` (3 keys). Handing off the second plan item after `i` is `i ↓ h` (3 keys). Opening the fifth search result is `s` + text + `↓↓↓↓` + Enter. `keys.test.tsx::every_action_within_two_keys` still passes because each action has a single key in the map, so S9 is reported as passing when it isn't.
findings.proposed_fix: Define "action" in the S9 test as a scripted main flow (S1 to S4, hand-off, sync), not a key-map entry, and count real keys in `claude plugin test`. Reserve a row-hotkey pool by cutting rarely used actions to `/room` (for example `c` curate, `t` remote, `w` who, `f` drift). Show at most 9 to 12 rows per page with letter or digit hotkeys, and have the engine rank lists so the item an action needs is first. Correct the entry claim to "`/room` then one key", or verify that a second `ctrl+x tab` reaches the pane.

findings.title: The Artifact transport can't serve most views, and synced edits don't appear on the remote map
findings.claim: The design says "Views can't tell which [transport] is in use", but the Artifact has only a static snapshot (default-lens maps, cards, diff summaries, plans, machines, who) and a `live/head` of summary frames. PathView, Anatomy, `show`/evidence text, diff hunks, the impact heat ramp, non-default lenses and `intent next` have no data source there, and no degraded or empty state is designed for them. After a sync smaller than 200 KB, `live/head` carries only `StreamFrame` summaries, so the viewer's own imported edit isn't reflected in the map they're looking at.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1122: "`artifact` (`./data/snapshot.json`, plus `db` `live/head` and `inbox/{self}`). Views can't tell which is in use." contracts.md:764-776: Snapshot fields include no breakdowns, paths, hunks or impact; `diffs: Vec<DiffSummary>`. architecture.md:1144: "evidence keeps `path` and `line` but not `contains`". contracts.md:777-778: `LiveHead.changes: Vec<StreamFrame>`, and contracts.md:260-261: frames carry only `{seq, kind, target, project, actor, status, summary}`. architecture.md:1147: "republishes the snapshot if more than 200 KB changed". artifact.md:5 / KICKOFF verified facts: "Pages can't call arbitrary hosts, so they can't reach the local server". KICKOFF R13: canvas "beautiful and fast on desktop and phone ... published as a Claude Artifact for when localhost isn't reachable". Principle 1: "Never show a blank state. ... Never lose or overwrite what someone did." feature_list S15's empty-state audit runs only against `planroom serve`, not the Artifact page.
findings.failure_scenario: On a phone (where localhost isn't reachable, so the Artifact is the only phone canvas), the person opens the Artifact and asks how storefront reaches worker. PathView's `query('ask', {path})` has no answer, so the view errors or renders blank. They rename `src/cart` to `cart-ui`. `/room sync` imports it, but under 200 KB changed, so there's no republish. On reload the map still shows `src/cart`, with only a summary line in `live/head`, and the edit looks lost.
findings.proposed_fix: Give `Transport` a declared capability set and have the snapshot carry it. On the Artifact, render controls for views with no snapshot data as an engine-authored empty state ("Needs your workspace: answered on the next sync") that queues an inbox `ask` request whose result the session writes to `results/<uid>`. Make `live/head` carry bounded data deltas (changed nodes and edges and their props) that the page applies over the snapshot, and keep an optimistic overlay of the viewer's own unacked rows until `acks/<uid>` confirms them. Add the Artifact page, with the fake db, to `empty_state_audit`.

findings.title: No designed pane or band state before the engine resolves or while it is down
findings.claim: On first use the engine is missing until a download or a source build of about 4 minutes finishes. The pane opens and draws from the `planroom.pane` atom, which only `planroom focus` fills, so the pane and band are blank throughout first run, and again whenever `focus` fails. The rule that "the engine authors every human-readable string" leaves the mod with no sanctioned text for these states, and the empty-state audit covers only the canvas.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1060: if the engine is missing, the mod starts `prefetch` and shows "Getting the Planroom engine..." only "in the status line". On failure it deals one card. architecture.md:1063-1064: the pane opens after the watch loop starts, and `planroom.pane` is written by a debounced `planroom focus --json`. architecture.md:1134 / DR-21: "Surfaces lay strings out; they never compose prose." feature_list S15: "every view visited on the empty workspace must render its empty.next action" (Playwright only). KICKOFF S14 (tier A): "The engine resolves on first use ... `/room` works". Principle 1: "Never show a blank state."
findings.failure_scenario: S14 fresh install: `/plugin install planroom@planroom`, then the session starts. The resolver finds no binary and starts a source build of about 4 minutes. The docked pane renders with an empty `PaneModel`: no focus, no card and no band. `/room` focuses an empty pane, and the only signal is a status-line string. If the build fails, the card has nowhere coherent to appear because the pane has no model.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a small bootstrap `PaneModel` that the mod draws when there's no engine or `focus` fails: engine state, progress, and one next action ("Build from source" or "Retry download"). Keep its strings in a generated subset of `en.toml` bundled into the mod at build time, so the strings still have one source. Add mounted-pane tests for the `missing`, `fetching`, `building`, `failed` and `schema_mismatch` states on all four surfaces.

findings.title: The phone-side sync trigger ("Send to Claude") isn't declared, and queued remote actions have no visible status
findings.claim: The page's "Send to Claude" trigger uses `comments.sendToClaude`, but the manifest declares only `db`, `user` and `sample`, so the button can't work. That leaves typed `/room sync` in the terminal as the only reliable trigger, and the phone user gets no feedback that their taps and edits are waiting.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1150: "the page's 'Send to Claude' button (`comments.sendToClaude`), which wakes the session". contracts.md:743-751: the capabilities are `db`, `user: {scopes:["profile"]}` and `sample: {}`, with no `comments`. artifact.md:149 and 212: `comments.sendToClaude` belongs to the `comments` capability and is writers-only. artifact.md:145: db writes don't wake the session. architecture.md:1152: a card tap becomes an inbox event, but no queued, synced or conflict state is designed on the page. KICKOFF `<design_starting_points>` Remote mode: "The Artifact shows cached decisions and queues new ones."
findings.failure_scenario: Away from the terminal, the person taps three cards and edits a name on the phone, then taps "Send to Claude". `claude.use('comments')` returns null and the button is hidden or fails. The cards still look actionable, so they tap again, which writes duplicate decide rows. Everything stays in the inbox until they return to the terminal and type `/room sync`, by which time the bases are stale and they get conflict cards.
findings.proposed_fix: Declare `comments: {}` in the manifest, and verify in WS7 that sendToClaude wakes the publishing session's watch. Have the page show each inbox row's state from `acks/<uid>` (queued, imported or conflict) and mark tapped cards as "queued". Have `/room sync` queue its model turn with `$.prompt.submit` rather than relying on returned context alone.

findings.title: The pane's row budget doesn't add up at the narrowest dock
findings.claim: The diff section is budgeted at 5 rows, but the contract asks for 3 one-liners plus a hunk of up to 5 lines, and the hunk needs a header line. The mini-map's "collapsed below 40 rows" doesn't say whether that means viewport rows or body rows. At 120×40 (viewport 40, body 34) the list section where search, hand-off and drill-down results appear can shrink to about 1 row.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1070-1079 budgets focus 3, decision 6, progress 1, diffs 5, drift 1, who 1, mini-map 8 to 12 ("collapsed below 40 rows"), with the list taking the rest. contracts.md:420: `diffs` are "top 3 one-liners, the first with up to 5 hunk lines", which is 3 + 1 header + 5 = 9 rows. mod-spike.md:22: `Code format="diff"` needs a valid hunk header. mod-spike.md:16: at 120x40, `bodyRows: 34`. mod-spike.md:31 budget has about 15 list rows, with no mini-map or drift row.
findings.failure_scenario: At 120×40, read as viewport rows, the mini-map shows: 3+6+1+9+1+1+12 = 33 of 34 body rows, so the list has 1 row and the `s` search Input pushes it off-screen. Read as body rows, the R13 mini-map is hidden by default on the narrowest dock.
findings.proposed_fix: State the threshold in body rows. At 34 body rows, cap the hunk at 2 lines (6 rows for diffs) and collapse the mini-map by default, so `m` reveals it in place of the list. Guarantee at least 10 list rows. Add a mounted-pane test at 49×34 that asserts the row total and the minimum list size.

findings.title: Light-mode chalk outlines are close to invisible on the mint felt
findings.claim: In light mode, the intended layer, the visual carrier of Intent and drift, is white at 80% over `#cfe6dc`, a contrast of about 1.25:1. Dashed outlines and "a block outside its outline" won't be readable, which weakens the S4 intended-vs-actual view. `--wait` text on the felt is also about 4.1:1.
findings.evidence: design-language.md:23 and 27: `--table` `#cfe6dc`, `--chalk` `#ffffff` at 80%. design-language.md:13: "Intended layer drawn as dashed chalk outlines; drift is a block outside its outline." Relative luminance is about 0.75 for the felt and about 0.95 for the chalk, which gives about 1.25:1. `--wait` `#7a6a12` on the felt gives about 4.15:1. KICKOFF look and feel asks for a "cohesive palette", and principle 1 says "Never make someone read what a ... diagram ... could show them instead."
findings.failure_scenario: At 1440×900 in light mode, after S4 step 1, the forbidden `worker -> orders-db` outline and the required `worker -> orders` chalk edge barely show against the felt. In the screenshot critique, the drift isn't visible without opening the diff tray.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a dark chalk in light mode (for example `--ink` at 55 to 65%, or a deep felt green like `#2d5a4a`) with a 2 px dash, keeping white chalk for dark mode. Add a token contrast check to `xtask check`: 3:1 for non-text marks and 4.5:1 for text tokens on `--table` and `--card`.

findings.title: The canvas doesn't say where the next action, Anatomy and Machine sit within the five concepts
findings.claim: S1 requires one suggested next action to be visible, but the canvas HUD maps `PaneModel` only to "breadcrumb, card, tray badge" and gives the next action no `data-concept` home. Anatomy (including a file outside the workspace, such as the S5 prompt snapshot) and Machine are said to be "reached from those five" with no entry point specified, so the S5 and S6 canvas evidence and the `exactly_five_concepts` audit have nothing to design against.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1111-1117: the five top-level controls, and "Views, all reached from those five". architecture.md:1128: PaneModel maps to "the HUD: breadcrumb, card, tray badge". architecture.md:1136 `same_output` expects the next-action text in the canvas DOM. architecture.md:1020: `breakdown` and `machine` "also take a file outside the workspace". KICKOFF S1: "one suggested next action". S15: "The UI exposes no top-level concepts beyond R14's five".
findings.failure_scenario: An M1 canvas track puts the next action in a floating top bar with no `data-concept`, and `exactly_five_concepts` fails. Or it adds a sixth "Next" control. For S5 evidence, nobody can open the kickoff snapshot's Anatomy from the canvas because there's no path input or entry point.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify that `PaneModel.next` renders as the face-up card in the Decisions stack when no decision is open, carrying `data-concept=decisions`. Specify Anatomy and Machine as Lenses (an `anatomy` lens on artifact blocks and a `machine` lens on machine nodes), and let breadcrumb search accept a path or `file:` reference for out-of-workspace files.

findings.title: No gesture map for phone: pinch zoom, level zoom, tap to focus and select overlap
findings.claim: On touch, the design leaves it open whether pinch changes the geometric scale or the level (the "lid lift" dive), what a tap does on a block (focus, select for an edit, or open evidence), how to zoom out a level, and how the five-concept HUD plus a bottom sheet fit 390 px with 44 px targets. S13 tests these gestures, but there's no spec to build them to.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1120: "390×844 with touch: 44 px targets, pinch-zoom and tap to focus, a bottom sheet for the tray and cards". design-language.md:11 and 58: Levels zoom "dives into a block" with a lid-lift motion. KICKOFF S13: "pinch-zoom and tap-to-focus work, and decision cards take one tap". KICKOFF look and feel: "Mobile-first".
findings.failure_scenario: Two tracks implement it differently. Pinch past a threshold triggers a level dive, so a pinch to read labels changes level unexpectedly. A tap on a block both focuses it and opens the bottom sheet, which covers the card stack. A person on the phone can't reliably get back up a level.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a gesture table to design-language.md: pinch and drag are geometric only, tap selects and focuses (ego view), the breadcrumb lid or a double-tap dives a level, the breadcrumb goes up, and a long-press opens evidence. Add a 390 px HUD wireframe (breadcrumb and lens switcher on top, card stack and tray in a two-detent bottom sheet). Cover each gesture in `quality.spec.ts`.

verdicts.reason: Import is an `any`-actor command exposed through `room_change`. It attributes rows by the local directory path, and the path is honoured for the owner's person-only commands. Nothing stops the chat model from writing files under `.planroom/share/inbox`: the `tool.check` guard covers only the person key and serve.json. So an agent can mint person-attributed decide or version events. That breaks R5, R8 and the design's own claim that "Person-only commands aren't reachable through tools at all".
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:237 `scan`, `import` | any | change | `room_change`. contracts.md:790 "person-only commands from the Artifact are allowed for the owner's own `uid`". architecture.md:1088 lists `import` among the room_change commands. architecture.md:387 / decisions.md:152: the guard covers only Bash, Read and Grep on `.planroom/person.key` or `serve.json`. No guard covers Write or Edit on share/inbox (grep for share/inbox finds only architecture.md:1147). The S11 test in feature_list.json covers only a forged body actor and harness-written rows, not agent-written rows.

verdicts.reason: The spike measured that a bare digit at the empty prompt presses the band's primary Button. `PaneModel.next` has no type constraint, and no document limits the band to reversible commands. `handoff merge` is person-only and repo-changing, and it has a pane key (`g`), so nothing stops `next` from pointing at it after `collect`. A stray leading '1' would then merge with the person key, which goes against principle 1 (everything is reversible) and R8 (merge follows a person's approval).
verdicts.evidence: mod-spike.md:18 "A bare digit at the empty prompt | Presses the mod's band Button". architecture.md:1081 "next best action as a primary Button with hotkey `1`". contracts.md:423 `pub next: Handle` with no constraint. architecture.md:983: merge runs `git merge --no-ff` in each repo. S15 undo assert in feature_list.json: "every Op x target kind, plus review, decision pick, version and claim" (no merge). KICKOFF.md:40 "Everything is reversible".

verdicts.reason: Several flows depend on `review` accept and reject: ghost items, inferred-fact confirmation (R2), the conflict card's "yours", the pane's y/n, and the S15 undo matrix. `review` is an event kind and a person-only rule, but it is not a `Command` variant or a CLI row. Batch acceptance runs through `decide CARD accept` (S3), which covers only part of it. `planroom open` and `/room open` are cited but appear in neither the enum nor the CLI table. The enum generates every surface, so these actions have no route.
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:200-213, the Command enum: no Review and no Open variant. architecture.md:1016-1031, the CLI table: no `review` or `open` row. architecture.md:327, 391, 410 rely on `review accept`. architecture.md:1049 "`planroom open` (the pane's `e` key)". architecture.md:153 `/room open`. contracts.md:736 ROOM_COMMANDS is limited to leaves plus share and sync. feature_list S3 uses `decide CARD accept` only for batches. The S15 assert includes "review" in the undo matrix.

verdicts.reason: Pane actions apply to the focused row or the first diff, and list rows have only arrows and Enter. So acting on the Nth item takes more than two keys from pane focus, and the planned test counts key-map entries, not real flows. The spike also shows `ctrl+x tab` focuses the band, not the pane, so one of the two entry routes in architecture.md is wrong. The interpretation of "action" can be argued, but the self-certifying test and the wrong entry claim are real, and S9 is tier B.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1079 "arrows, `Enter` opens" for the list. architecture.md:1081 "(`/room` or `ctrl+x tab`, then one hotkey)". mod-spike.md:19 "`ctrl+x tab` | Focuses the band". mod-api.md:158 "at most 36 one-key actions per pane". The S9 test step in feature_list.json is "a keystroke-count table generated from the pane's key map".

verdicts.reason: The Artifact transport claims parity ("Views can't tell which is in use"), but the Snapshot carries only default-lens maps, cards, diff summaries, plans, machines, who and the pane. PathView, impact, Anatomy, show/evidence text and hunks have no source. `live/head` changes are StreamFrame summaries, so a synced edit isn't reflected in the map until a republish, and that happens only above 200 KB. The canvas's optimistic pending store lasts only until the edit is confirmed. Remote views would therefore be blank or stale, which goes against principle 1 and affects S11 and R13 on the phone.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1122 "Views can't tell which is in use". contracts.md:764-776 Snapshot fields. contracts.md:777-778 `changes: Vec<StreamFrame>`. contracts.md:259-260: frames carry `summary` only. architecture.md:1147 "republishes the snapshot if more than 200 KB changed". architecture.md:1121 "Pending edits survive a reload in `sessionStorage` ... until confirmed". The S15 empty-state audit in feature_list.json runs on the empty workspace through Playwright on serve, not on the Artifact page.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real: the card's host and the mod-authored strings are unspecified while the engine is missing. But the wiring order means the pane opens only after the watch loop starts (step 5 after step 4, which needs the binary), so no blank docked pane is drawn during the build. The status line shows "Getting the Planroom engine..." with progress. The S14 tier A asserts (resolves on first use, `/room` works afterwards) don't fail. This is a design gap in bootstrap UX, not a material violation.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1060 "If it's missing, start `prefetch` ... show 'Getting the Planroom engine...' in the status line. If the fetch fails, deal one card ... with progress in the status line". architecture.md:1063-1064: step 4 spawns `[bin, "watch", ...]`, and step 5 then opens the pane. decisions.md:494 DR-28 has the same wording. The S14 asserts in feature_list.json don't cover the pane during the build.

verdicts.reason: The design relies on `comments.sendToClaude` as a sync trigger, but the manifest omits the `comments` capability, so that trigger can't work as specified. The page has no queued, imported or conflict state per row, although `acks/<uid>` exists. The finding is already rated minor, and that fits.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1150 "the page's 'Send to Claude' button (`comments.sendToClaude`)". contracts.md:743-751: the capabilities are db, user and sample only. artifact.md:149: sendToClaude belongs to comments and is writers-only. artifact.md:212 also places it under `comments`.

verdicts.reason: Recomputed: white at 80% over #cfe6dc composites to about rgb(245,250,248), with luminance about 0.946 against about 0.750 for the felt, a contrast of about 1.25:1. So light-mode chalk outlines, the Intent and drift carrier, are close to invisible. The finding is already rated minor, which fits.
verdicts.evidence: design-language.md:24 `--table` `#cfe6dc`. design-language.md:28 `--chalk` `#ffffff` at 80%. design-language.md:13 "Intended layer drawn as dashed chalk outlines; drift is a block outside its outline". Relative-luminance calculation: (0.946+0.05)/(0.750+0.05) is about 1.245.

verdicts.reason: The phone spec is one line: "pinch-zoom and tap to focus, a bottom sheet". The documents never settle whether pinch is geometric zoom or a level dive, what a tap means compared with selection or evidence, or how to go back up a level on touch. design-language describes the level zoom as a lid-lift dive with no touch gesture. This is a real spec gap, rated minor.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1120 "390×844 with touch: 44 px targets, pinch-zoom and tap to focus, a bottom sheet for the tray and cards". design-language.md:11 "Zoom dives into a block". design-language.md:51 "A level zoom. The block's lid lifts". No gesture table exists in the documents.
